items.rule: Project restores, stewards or assesses wetland or floodplain easements
items.quote: The types of work available through this opportunity fall into three primary categories: 1) restoration of wetland and floodplain easements; 2) stewardship of wetland and floodplain easements, and 3) onsite and offsite assessment of easement conditions.

items.rule: Not a foreign organization or foreign public entity
items.quote: Foreign organizations and foreign public entities
Eligibility for this opportunity is limited to non-Federal entities.

items.rule: Not debarred, suspended or otherwise excluded from federal awards
items.quote: Are not debarred, suspended, or otherwise excluded from receiving Federal awards

items.rule: No federal felony conviction in the 24 months before accepting the award
items.quote: It has not been convicted of a felony criminal violation under any Federal law within the preceding 24 months.

items.rule: No finalized unpaid federal tax liability unless paying on time under an agreed payment plan
items.quote: It has no unpaid Federal tax liability that has been assessed, for which all judicial and administrative remedies have been exhausted or have lapsed, and that is not being paid in a timely manner pursuant to an agreement with the authority responsible for collecting the tax liability;

items.rule: Has active System for Award Management (SAM) registration
items.quote: Have an active System for Award Management (SAM) registration (2 CFR part 25).

items.rule: Maintains written standards of conduct covering conflicts of interest
items.quote: 2 CFR 400.2 states that applicants must maintain written standards of conduct covering conflicts of interest and governing the performance of its employees in the selection, award, and administration of Federal awards.
The project narrative must not exceed eight (8) pages.
The Project Abstract must not exceed one page and must contain a summary of the proposed activity suitable for dissemination to the public.
Budget Information for Non-Construction Programs (SF-424A)
Click here to add the mandatory Budget Narrative. Required.

items.item: Key personnel resumes with relevant licences and certifications
items.quote: Resumes for key personnel in an appendix to the proposal including any related licenses or certifications the applicant’s project personnel possess and for which states they are valid

items.item: Current and pending support statements for each key person
items.quote: Submit a Statement of Current and Pending Support for each key personnel who will participate in the project.
Include GADSUM-9, Applicant Contact(s) Information; see 7.1 that follows.
Is the Certification Regarding Lobbying attached (see section V.9.)?

items.item: Current NICRA, if indirect costs are allowed and the organization has one
items.quote: If indirect costs are allowable and the organization has a NICRA, attach the current NICRA as an optional attachment.

items.item: Subaward budget details and narratives, if subawards are planned
items.quote: If the applicant’s budget includes funding for a subaward(s), is a PDF attachment included for each subaward that contains a Subaward Budget Detail (see section V.8.1.1) and a budget narrative?

steps.quote: Application deadline: Submit via Grants.gov by 11:59 pm Eastern Time on November 19, 2026.
The agency validation process includes meeting eligibility requirements and following the application guidelines (e.g., formatting, page limitations, limits on budget requests).
A merit/technical review will be conducted by a technical review board.
Risk reviews will be conducted by the FPAC-BC, Grants and Agreements Division (GAD). The approving official will make the final award decisions.

The Notice of Grant and Agreement Award (ADS-093) contains information identified in 2 CFR 200.211 and is signed by the authorized agency official; it is the only authorizing document and will be provided electronically to the entity’s authorized official for signature.

co_finance.quote: There is no cost sharing requirement for this opportunity.

consortium.quote: “Partnerships” or other similar groupings (i.e., application must be submitted by a single entity; a partner may serve as a subrecipient).

items.quote: The awardee will also provide NRCS monthly status report of work in progress and any other documentation that may be identified as required by the NRCS standards and specifications or agreement terms and conditions.

All non-federal entities that expend $1,000,000 or more in Federal awards during the non-Federal entity’s fiscal year must have a single or program-specific audit conducted for that year, in accordance with the provisions of 2 CFR 200.501.

Any official site visit on the premises of a recipient or a subrecipient(s) requires that the recipient provide, and must require its subrecipients to provide, all reasonable facilities and assistance in order for the USDA awarding agency representatives to perform their duties.
The training required will be provided by NRCS.

answer.notes: Checked the FY2026 MOD01 notice listed as updated October 19, 2026; the supplied PDF is identical. The call-attached application guide is dated October 1, 2024. The newer October 1, 2026 guide removes Current and Pending Support, but the amended NOFO still requires it and takes precedence. The ten-document limit leaves two additional submissions to note: written disclosure of potential conflicts of interest, if any, and SF-LLL if lobbying activities occurred. No pre-application or letter of intent should be submitted. Further documents may be requested during administrative review. Supported easements include ACEP-WRE, WRP and EWPP-FPE; specific easements are identified during selection. Profit is ineligible, and nonprofit and higher-education cooperative agreements cap indirect costs at 10% of total direct costs. Paid participating producers must meet 7 CFR Parts 12 and 1400, control the land for the project period, and have AGI no greater than $900,000 unless waived; this is not an applicant revenue cap. Tax and felony certifications apply when accepting the award. Monthly reporting is coded as quarterly because the schema includes more frequent reporting; final performance and financial reports are also required. The audit threshold concerns annual expenditure of all federal awards. Site-visit cooperation applies if a visit occurs; training is specified for easement monitoring. General terms are those in effect when the award is executed. Only the April 2023 monitoring manual was read; the current update could not be verified.
